guard_streams.source: Automatic compensation: What you need to know

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the automatic-compensation guidance on 20 July 2026.
Customers of participating broadband and landline providers can receive compensation automatically when qualifying service failures occur.
The guidance lists BT, EE, Hyperoptic, Plusnet, Sky including NOW Broadband, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media, Vodafone and Zen Internet.
Delayed repair following a loss of service is one of the qualifying situations described.
Compensation amounts increase annually in line with inflation.

guard_streams.source: Making a complaint and using alternative dispute resolution (ADR) schemes

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the ADR guidance on 20 July 2026.
Customers should first contact their provider's customer services and then make a formal complaint if the issue is not resolved.
ADR schemes are free independent bodies that make impartial assessments of unresolved complaints.
A complaint can be taken to ADR after at least six weeks or earlier when a deadlock letter has been issued.
Ofcom approves CISAS and Communications Ombudsman as the two ADR schemes listed on the page.

guard_streams.source: Are you in or out of contract?

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the contract-status guidance on 17 July 2026.
Phone, broadband and pay-TV contracts are typically 12, 18 or 24 months long.
Leaving before the contract ends can trigger an early termination charge.
End-of-contract notifications must be sent between 10 and 40 days before the contract ends.
Providers must remind customers who remain out of contract every year and update them on best available deals.

guard_streams.source: Use an Ofcom-accredited price comparison site to find the best deal

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the accredited price-comparison guidance on 17 July 2026.
Ofcom-accredited comparison sites are put through an audit.
The audit checks accessibility, accuracy, transparency, comprehensiveness and currency of information.
The listed accredited services cover combinations of broadband, mobile, landline and pay-TV products.
The page lists accredited services including broadbandchoices.co.uk, MoneySuperMarket.com, Broadband Genie and broadbanddeals.co.uk.

guard_streams.source: Telecoms price rises – what are your rights?

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the price-rise guidance on 29 June 2026.
Since January 2025, new contracts cannot include inflation-linked or percentage-based price rises.
Specified in-contract price rises must be stated clearly in pounds and pence before sign-up.
When an increase was not specified or exceeds the agreed amount, the provider must give at least 30 days' notice and a 30-day exit window.
Contracts signed before 17 January 2025 may still contain inflation-linked or percentage-based increases.
